definitions.explanation: A physical document that certifies ownership of shares in a company. In modern Japan, most shares are managed electronically.

examples.japanese: {株券|かぶけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発行|はっこう}する→発行する：19236_hakkousuru⟧。
⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遺品|いひん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{株券|かぶけん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧きた。
examples.english: Old stock certificates were found among my grandfather's belongings.

examples.japanese: 2009⟦{年|ねん}→年：09876_nen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{株券|かぶけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電子化|でんしか}→電子化：15001_denshika⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{完了|かんりょう}→完了：02560_kanryou⟧し、⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{株券|かぶけん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{原則|げんそく}→原則：11801_gensoku⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The digitization of stock certificates was completed in 2009, and paper certificates were abolished in principle.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{株|かぶ}→株：02592_kabu⟧ (stock, shares) and ⟦{券|けん}→券：02150_ken⟧ (certificate, ticket). Historically, {株券|かぶけん} were important physical documents proving share ownership. In Japan, the shift to electronic share management ({株券|かぶけん}⟦{電子化|でんしか}→電子化：15001_denshika⟧) was completed in January 2009, making paper certificates largely obsolete.

Old paper {株券|かぶけん} are occasionally found during estate settlements and may still have value if the issuing company exists.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {株券|かぶけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{発行|はっこう}する→発行する：19236_hakkousuru⟧: to issue stock certificates
- {株券|かぶけん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電子化|でんしか}→電子化：15001_denshika⟧: digitization of stock certificates
- {株券|かぶけん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{保管|ほかん}する→保管する：25536_hokansuru⟧: to store stock certificates
- ⟦{紙|かみ}→紙：00712_kami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{株券|かぶけん}: paper stock certificate

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{株|かぶ}→株：02592_kabu⟧: stock; shares — the shares themselves, not the physical certificate
- {有価証券|ゆうかしょうけん}: securities — the broader category including stocks, bonds, and other financial instruments
- ⟦{社債|しゃさい}→社債：24079_shasai⟧: corporate bond — a different type of security representing debt, not ownership
